name: Silk PLA
chemical_makeup: PLA-majority blend with a small fraction of thermoplastic-elastomer / polyester-type gloss additive that raises surface sheen and adds slight melt elasticity; sometimes co-extruded as a dual-colour strand for a shifting sheen
summary: Base PLA with a gloss additive package — same lactide chemistry, aesthetic delta only. Versus base PLA it runs 10-20 °C hotter and slower for maximum sheen (210-240 °C vs 190-230 °C), is denser (1.27 vs 1.24 g/cm³), noticeably more moisture-sensitive, and has markedly worse layer adhesion (Z tensile 25 MPa vs XY 33 MPa) and low elongation (2.8 % XY), so it is a display material, not a structural one.

printing.notes: Delta vs base PLA: run 10-20 °C hotter. Bambu's Silk/Silk+ TDS gives 210-240 °C (specimens tested near 230 °C) against 190-230 °C for base PLA, and rates the material to 250 mm/s — but gloss is directly controlled by temperature (higher) and speed (lower), so community practice is 30-60 mm/s on outer walls for the best sheen. Unfilled, so no hardened nozzle. As with base PLA, open the door/lid on an enclosed machine.

feeding.notes: Rigid filament, so any extruder feeds it and no spool-side assistant is needed. Bambu's material table still lists Silk/Silk+ as AMS-compatible, but this is 'conditional' rather than base PLA's plain 'yes': the elastomer content makes the strand more prone to delamination under tension and forum users report layer-adhesion failures and occasional grip problems specifically when feeding silk PLA through an AMS on an X1C. Run it from an external spool for critical long prints.

drying.dryness_validation: Test-print a large smooth curved surface and inspect under raking light: micro-bubbles, a dulled or milky sheen, or stringing mean it is still wet. No popping or steam at the nozzle.
drying.notes: Delta vs base PLA (45-55 °C / 4-8 h): Bambu specifies 55 °C for 8 h in a blast oven, or 65-75 °C for 12 h using a heated bed. Moisture damage shows up cosmetically here long before it shows up mechanically — surface bubbling and a dull finish defeat the entire point of the material.

storage.recommendations: Sealed bag or drybox with desiccant between prints; treat more strictly than base PLA because moisture ruins the gloss before it ruins the part

price.notes: Bambu PLA Silk+ around $22.99/kg; comparable to or slightly above base PLA Basic at roughly $18-20/kg

recommended: gifts and giveaway prints where finish sells the part
not_recommended: snap-fit and clip geometry (low elongation, brittle)
parts loaded in Z (weak layer bonding)

properties.notes: Bambu PLA Silk TDS: density 1.27 g/cm³ (vs 1.24 for base PLA), tensile XY 33±4 MPa and Z 25±4 MPa, elongation XY 2.8±0.6 % and Z 1.5±0.2 %, Tg 57 °C, HDT 60 °C at 0.45 MPa and 56 °C at 1.8 MPa. Thermally it matches base PLA; mechanically it is both weaker and far more brittle than base PLA's 45-65 MPa, and the XY/Z gap is the practical story — the gloss additive costs layer bonding. Bambu's 'PLA Silk+' is marketed as a strengthened revision of the original Silk; figures here are for the Silk family generally.

compatibility.notes: Same PLA-family bonding behaviour as the base entry: welds to itself and other PLA grades, does not weld to PETG/ABS/ASA/PC/PA/PP. Because interfaces are the weak point of this grade, keep multi-material seams out of load paths. Standard PLA supports work; use PVA/BVOH where a glossy underside must be preserved.

plate_recommendations.notes: Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Smooth PEI mirrors the silk sheen onto the first layer — the main reason to choose smooth over textured for silk.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Same as base PLA; the mirror-smooth glass bottom pairs well with silk's sheen.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Specialty PLA blends behave as base PLA on this surface; the laminate's grip does not over-bond silk the way tacky low-temp surfaces can.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Bottom face reads as soft satin rather than mirror; use smooth PEI if you want the silk gloss underneath.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Silk grades that over-bond on tacky low-temp plates behave normally here — thermal release does the work, not surface tack.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Adhesion is unproblematic, but the texture transfers to the bottom face and destroys the silk sheen there.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Silk and metallic PLA are the standout pairing — the reflective surface amplifies the diffraction pattern.

Adheres fine at 35-45 °C, but the textured surface transfers its grain to the bottom layer and kills the silk sheen there. For parts whose underside is visible, a smooth PEI or glass surface is preferred — this is the one plate-choice delta versus base PLA, where textured PEI is simply recommended.

Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): Bambu's own wiki warns that its PLA Silk bonds so hard to SuperTack that removal may damage the printed model. Third-party silk PLAs vary but should be treated the same until teste

emissions.notes: No measured difference from base PLA; the elastomer/gloss fraction is small and no unusual fumes are reported. Printing 10-20 °C hotter than base PLA nudges particulate emission up slightly, so ventilate for continuous printing in an occupied room.

safety_notes: Colourant and gloss-additive package is not food-contact certified — treat silk parts as decorative only, including for dry food.
additional_notes: Gloss is a process outcome, not just a material property: temperature up and speed down both increase sheen. Dual-colour co-extruded silk spools shift hue with viewing angle and are a separate marketing category from gradient (colour-along-length) filament — see pla-gradient.

provenance.conflicts: AMS compatibility: Bambu's general material table lists Silk/Silk+ as AMS-compatible, while Bambu forum users report layer-adhesion and feed problems specific to AMS routing — recorded as 'conditional'. Drying: Bambu gives 55 °C/8 h (blast oven) or 65-75 °C/12 h (heated bed), noticeably hotter than the 45-55 °C used for base PLA; both are listed rather than reconciled. Mechanical figures are Bambu's Silk TDS; 'Silk+' is claimed to be stronger but no separate numbers were located, so the improvement is unverified.
